thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow's Bid For 7th-straight Winning Session In Play

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow's Bid For 7th-straight Winning Session In Play
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Shares of The Trade Desk, Nvidia, Dropbox, PPG could be active
U.S. stock futures were trading higher on Friday, with the Dow industrials poised to post the longest winning streak since late last year, as investors breathed a bit easier over inflation and dollar's swift pace of gains slowed.
Investors will hear from a Federal Reserve official and get updates on import prices and consumer sentiment.
What are markets doing?
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures rose 60 points, or 0.2%, to 24,750, while S&P 500 futures rose 6.3 points, or 0.2%, to 2,725. Nasdaq-100 futures turned higher, rising 9 points, or 0.1%, to 6,965.25.
On Thursday, the Dow industrials logged a sixth-straight positive session (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-set-for-6th-straight-day-of-gains-as-traders-look-to-inflation-data-2018-05-10), the longest stretch in more than two months, rising 196.99 points, or 0.8%, to 24,739.53. A positive close Friday would make for the longest winning streak since the one that ended the week of Nov. 8, 2017.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite Index each logged gains of 0.9% on Thursday. The tech-heavy index closed higher for a fifth straight session, its longest such streak since February.
For the week, stocks are poised to gain across the board. As of Thursday, the Dow was up 0.8%, the S&P 500 was up 2.2% and the Nasdaq was up 2.7%.
Read:Here's why the stock market has its swagger back -- for now (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-why-he-stock-market-has-its-swagger-backfor-now-2018-05-10)
What is driving the markets?
Cooler U.S. consumer prices (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/consumer-inflation-softer-than-expected-in-april-cpi-shows-2018-05-10) helped propel stocks Thursday, while lower bond yields and a weak dollar also lent a hand. Meanwhile, Wall Street's so-called "fear gauge" has been falling for the past five sessions, tapping its lowest level since late January (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wall-streets-fear-index-drops-to-levels-not-seen-since-before-stocks-fell-in-to-correction-2018-05-10).
On Friday, data on import prices for April are due at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, while the University of Michigan's consumer-sentiment index for May is expected at 10 a.m.
St. Louis Fed President James Bullard is due to deliver a speech on economic and monetary policy to the Springfield Area Chamber of Commerce in Springfield, Mo., at 8:30 a.m.
What are strategists saying?
"The important question is whether investors will look to take some profits off the table at this time, allowing the greenback to retreat slightly, but more importantly whether they will treat any pullback as an opportunity to buy the dip. In simpler terms, does the slowdown in inflation seen yesterday kill the chances for the Fed moving toward more rate hikes this year?" said Konstantinos Anthis, head of research at ADS Securities, in a note to clients.
Read:First-quarter earnings season was great--except for this small thing (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/first-quarter-earnings-season-was-greatexcept-for-this-small-thing-2018-05-10)
What stocks are in focus?
The Trade Desk Inc.(TTD) jumped 23% in premarket after the platform for managing digital-ad campaigns blew out earnings forecasts. It reported that streaming TV advertising surged nearly 2,000% over the year in the first quarter.
Read:CEO of Trade Desk sees rapidly increased spending on connected TV ads (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trade-desk-stock-skyrockets-as-ad-spending-on-streaming-tv-goes-up-2000-2018-05-10)
Shares of Nvidia Corp.(NVDA) fell 2% in premarket after the chip maker's shares fell in late trade, even after the company reported results and an outlook that topped Wall Street's view (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/nvidias-stock-eases-back-from-record-high-following-big-earnings-beat-strong-outlook-2018-05-10).

(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dropbox-earnings-beat-expectations-after-ipo-but-stock-still-dips-2018-05-10)Shares of PPG Industries Inc.(PPG) could come under pressure after the paint maker fired its controller and reassigned employees (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ppg-industries-fires-controller-as-it-finds-more-accounting-mistakes-2018-05-10) as it said it found additional accounting errors worth millions.
Apple Inc.(AAPL) and Goldman Sachs Group Inc.(GS) could be in focus after a report in The Wall Street Journal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-and-goldman-sachs-in-joint-credit-card-venture-2018-05-10) are preparing to launch a new joint credit card.
Drug stocks could be active ahead after the administration of President Donald Trump is expected to make a speech on drug prices (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/five-things-to-expect-again-from-president-trumps-upcoming-drug-price-speech-2018-04-19) on Friday.
What are other markets doing?
Asian markets (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-stock-markets-mostly-rise-as-cooler-us-inflation-reading-inspires-risk-on-buying-2018-05-10) finished the week mostly higher, except for a 0.3% drop for the Shanghai Composite Index , while European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-hover-around-3-month-high-as-metal-producers-rise-2018-05-11) were pushing toward a seventh-straight weekly win.
Oil futures were mostly flat, with West Texas Intermediate crude up 7 cents to $71.42 a barrel, but still poised to gain 2% for the week.

The dollar was down 0.2% to 92.469, while gold inched higher.
